mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 5.25%, or the effect is insignificant in a 5-year rolling window (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market softness reduces growth expectations while inflation moderation boosts equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakening with cooling inflation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or insignificant when the interaction pattern is present, or the correlation between the proxies falls below 0.5 in a 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% year-over-year is accompanied by a 1-month lag in S&P 500 returns, indicating strong demand that is already reflected in equity prices, thus predicting a negative 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO > +2% YoY, or the effect is absent in a 200-day rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential construction (assumed proxy via HOUST) for three consecutive months predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as weak building activity signals an over-supplied housing market and reduced risk aversion.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when HOUST declines for three consecutive months, or the effect is not significant in a 12-month test.

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in three months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 20-day forward return as lower labor market friction supports economic growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% after a 3-month trend decline
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or the effect is not robust across 10 such episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both retail sales (implied via PAYEMS) and manufacturing (INDPRO) above their 2023 Q4 averages for two consecutive months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to over-heating demand and risk of a soft landing failure.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and INDPRO both exceed 2023 Q4 averages for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the interaction persists, or the effect is absent in a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 jobs with no change in CPIAUCSL suggests strong labor absorption without price pressure, predicting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return in a non-inflationary regime.
regime_hint: labor market expansion without inflationary pressure
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the interaction pattern is present, or the effect is not significant in a 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for four consecutive months in a tightening regime is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as markets price in lower future inflation risk.
regime_hint: low inflation in a tightening environment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive when CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for four months without a corresponding equity rally, or the effect is not significant in a 2-year test.
